browserLoadFailure.rootCauseAssessment: transformers.js ^3.0.0 bundles ONLY the jsep-enabled onnxruntime-web wasm build (dist/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.jsep.mjs/.wasm -- verified, no plain non-jsep alternative ships in that package). That single binary appears to perform WebGPU capability/adapter negotiation at pipeline-load time regardless of the requested `device` option, and hard-fails when no adapter exists at all -- even for an explicit device:'wasm' request. This is an environment limitation (this sandbox's headless Chromium has zero WebGPU adapter), not evidence against yolos-tiny's architecture: this repo's own CLAUDE.md documents yolos-tiny running successfully on webgpu in a real (non-headless) Chrome session. Contrast: raw onnxruntime-web (not wrapped by transformers.js) DID gracefully tolerate the missing adapter for UltraFace's session (see ultraface.webgpuRequested above) -- so this is specifically a transformers.js/jsep-bundle limitation, not a Chromium or ONNX Runtime one.

nodeCpuRecallFallback.note: onnxruntime-node CPU fp32 -- recall evidence ONLY, NOT a browser latency comparison Run via onnxruntime-node (@huggingface/transformers' Node backend), CPU, fp32, the same local yolos-tiny weights extension/models/Xenova/yolos-tiny ships, same threshold=0.5/percentage=false as extension/src/offscreen.entry.js. Detection correctness (recall) does not depend on which CPU/GPU backend executed the model, only latency does -- so these are valid recall numbers despite not being a browser measurement. The `ms` fields here are onnxruntime-node timings on 1280x720 inputs and are NOT comparable to any browser WASM/WebGPU number -- not used for the latency leg of the decision rule.

publishedProductionLatency.note: v1's own docs flag the 780-880ms figure as unresolved/does-not-reproduce as of 2026-09-20; the most recent independent samples cluster ~2650-2700ms warm. Both cited unmodified as the pre-registered ARCHITECTURE.md V0b baseline ('current published yolos warm: ~2,350-2,700 ms').

decision.rule: ARCHITECTURE.md Phase V0b, pre-registered: replace yolos-tiny iff UltraFace detects the demo face AND every >=80px face, AND its warm p95 is lower than yolos. Keep yolos available only if it catches something UltraFace cannot that is PII-relevant.
decision.verdict: REPLACE yolos-tiny with UltraFace RFB-320 for face redaction
decision.yolosCatchesSomethingUltrafaceMissesNote: Not observed in this fixture set: every scale where yolos-person fired (96px, 200px), UltraFace also fired, and UltraFace additionally caught 80px and 120px where yolos missed. yolos was non-monotonic across scale (hit 96px, missed 120px) -- unreliable as a size signal. Design-level caveat, not measured here (all fixtures are forward-facing face crops): yolos's COCO 'person' class detects full-body/torso silhouettes and could in principle fire on a person whose face is occluded, turned away, or too small to resolve as a face, which a face-only detector like UltraFace structurally cannot. No fixture in this spike exercises that case.
